text: The Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF), a tax-exempt organization established in 1987 and renamed in 2006, serves 55 member institutions across the U.S. and Virgin Islands, operating independently of the UNCF. Its portfolio includes 42 primary HBCUs, two law schools, two medical schools, two Public Benefit Institutions, and one junior college, with endowments ranging from under $1 million to over $700 million and student populations from approximately 600 to over 13,000. Academically, most members compete in NCAA Division I (FCS) or Division II within conferences such as the SWAC, MEAC, CIAA, and SIAC. Geographically distributed across the South, Midwest, Northeast, and Virgin Islands, TMCF is backed by significant corporate funding from entities like Apple and The Boeing Company, and expanded through the 2013 acquisition of Opportunity Funding Corporation. Under the leadership of Harry L. Williams since 2018, the fund focuses on institutional support, capacity building, and scholarships. Regarding specific athletic affiliations, North Carolina A&T competes in the CAA Football conference.
